passage.title: Rizq Foods Ltd: stock control
paras: Rizq Foods' production line makes 4,800 halal ready meals a day with 12 workers. It keeps two weeks of chilled and frozen ingredients in a large cold store, which costs £30,000 a year to run. Last year £18,000 of ingredients passed their use-by date and were thrown away.

A manager wants to introduce just-in-time (JIT) stock control: ingredients delivered daily, used straight away. Its main chicken supplier is 15 miles away and has been late four times this year. In January, snow closed the motorway for a day.
passage.source: All businesses, people and figures in this case are fictional, made up for practice.

blocks.h: Answer frame (12 marks: both sides, then a supported judgement)

blocks.text: 'Rizq Foods should introduce just-in-time stock control.' Evaluate this statement. (12 marks)

frame.label: For: point and chain of reasoning in context
Against: point and chain of reasoning in context
Judgement
frame.prompt: Decide, give the main reason, and say what it depends on.

markScheme.a: For: saves most of the £30,000 cold-store cost and the £18,000 of waste, freeing cash and space; fresher ingredients. Against: depends on daily deliveries; the supplier was late four times and snow closed the motorway; one lost day costs about £14,000 of sales and may break supermarket contracts. Judgement: it depends on supplier reliability; e.g. use JIT for some ingredients with a small buffer stock. Level 4 (10-12): developed chains of reasoning on both sides in context, and a supported judgement with 'it depends on'. Level 3 (7-9): both sides developed, judgement partly supported. Level 2 (4-6): some development, one-sided or generic. Level 1 (1-3): points identified.
